note: Stockton Lake Corps campground in two parts a cove apart. North holds the electric sites: the B loop on a wooded point with the lake on three sides, and the A loop around an open field by the swim beach. South (C and D loops) is non-electric. No site has a water hookup. The lake shows through the hardwoods from the point sites, across the loop road; no site is on the shore. --Claude
summary: Confirmed on rec.gov: 60 individual sites (not 118), 30 with 50A, no water hookups; season Mar 15-Nov 30 with reduced shoulder seasons; fees $10-32; 3-night holiday minimum. Lakeview kept (filtered). Pin is the rec.gov facility point, on no loop: move proposed. Split candidate reported. Phone to add.
flags: PIN MOVE (1.0 km): stored 37.6594,-93.7831 is the rec.gov facility point; on imagery it is wooded shore on the southern peninsula, on no camp loop (the nearest sites, D loop, are ~500 m west). Proposed 37.66835,-93.78470, the centre of the B loop (18 electric sites) in the North campground. The A loop (25 sites, 12 electric) is centred 37.6738,-93.7822.

SPLIT CANDIDATE (owner's call): rec.gov sells one facility in two loops records, NORT (A+B, 43 sites, all 30 electric ones) and SOUT (C+D, 17 non-electric sites plus the group camp). On imagery the South loops (centre 37.6620,-93.7905) are ~850 m from the B loop across a marina cove and ~1.5 km from the A loop, reached by a different road along the southern peninsula with its own attendant booth (notice: 'park attendent booth. Located at the entrance of C and D loop'); the North loops come off the road to the swim beach. campgrounds.json has no other entry within 2.5 km (nearest 1871 Crabtree Cove). It meets the distance-and-own-entrance test only just (850 m to B), and the South is a 17-site non-electric annex, so it is reported rather than proposed outright.

WATERFRONT (stored lakeview, kept; on the weak side): no site is within 50 m of the water on an open apron. B loop: the pads sit inside the loop road on a wooded point, the shore 40-80 m away on three sides beyond the road and a belt of hardwoods (leaf-off imagery; the two tip sites B01/B02 carry a premium rate). A loop electric sites back onto timber around an open field, the lake 120 m+ away through woods - no view shown. C/D loops are wooded, 40-90 m above the shore. rec.gov gives no 'Proximity to Water' attribute on any site. Site photos were not viewed, so the view is from imagery only: filtered through trees in leaf.

COUNT: the catalog has 60 individual sites + 1 group camp; the facility text and the stored note say 118. C sites below C11 and several D numbers are absent from the catalog (pads still visible on imagery).
PHONE (none stored): rec.gov gives the park at 417-276-6948 and the Stockton project office at 417-276-3113.
The USACE Stockton Lake page was not fetched (district pages refuse plain fetches); everything here is from recreation.gov.
